correctness.rationale: The algebra is generated by e₁, and bracket preservation forces f(e_j)=a₁^(j−1) times the shift by j−1 of f(e₁). The resulting matrix is triangular with diagonal a₁^j, so it is invertible exactly for a₁≠0. Conversely these maps preserve the defining products (left factors e_j with j≥2 still have no first-coordinate component). Composition in the polynomial model gives the stated scaling action. For scalar a of order d prime to p, the d-th root of the norm is a projection to U^a. Its kernel is the image of w↦w/ρ_a(w): this image has norm one and index |U^a|, the same index as the norm kernel. Conjugation by principal units removes exactly this kernel, giving the count factor q^(n−1−h_{d,0}). Frobenius raises each monomial exponent by the factor p^t, with no cross terms and with injective coefficient Frobenius. Thus the coefficients of all x^(dj) with dj p^t≤n−1 must vanish for order dividing p^t, including the t=0 case. Subtracting successive torsion counts gives N. On the reduced coordinate in U^a, conjugation by scalars is the only remaining action; it commutes with the projection. A centralizing pair (w,b) must have w∈U^a and b in the scalar stabilizer since the norm-kernel and fixed factors intersect trivially. For a second scalar of order e, exponents fixed by both are exactly the multiples of lcm(d,e), giving the stated fixed torsion count, and Burnside on exact-order strata gives K and its total. The unit 1+x has order p^E, and the scalar subgroup has order q−1, proving the exponent via the lcm. The d=q−1 stratum has n−1<d p^E, so its top p-part occurs iff d p^(E−1)≤n−1. This includes q=2 and n=2. RESULT.md lines 4–72 and the bundled verification notes and script were inspected, not run. Separately, direct multiplication and conjugation in the specified model checked 41 strata across nine cases over q=2,3,4,5 (including both class and element counts over the extension field F₄); replay is python3 independent_census.py, with recorded output in independent_census_run.txt. For (q,n)=(5,3), classes by order 1,2,4,5,10 are 1,1,2,7,2 and the exponent 20 is not attained. The finite check uses the group model and does not prove it or the arbitrary-parameter formulas.

originality.rationale: The prior structural theorem is credited, including the unit subgroup and diagonal complement. The supported distinct claim is the joint finite-field exact-order/element-class census and resulting exponent-attainment criterion in this group. The inspected primary results do not evaluate these invariants, and the closest catalogue spectra count different groups or different objects. The exact counts require tracking which unit exponents survive two simultaneous scalar symmetries and a Frobenius power, rather than reparameterizing a known order or class count.
residual_risks: Bounded statement-level searches do not exclude an older treatment in the finite-group literature of these truncated-unit scalar semidirect products. The group description itself is not credited as new.

value.rationale: Exact element orders and conjugacy classes are basic group invariants; counting classes separately by exact order gives more than either group size or a class total. The uniform arithmetic formulas resolve these invariants across dimensions and prime powers, and decide a natural structural boundary: the exponent of the group can be unattained. They give exact results where enumerating all matrices and all conjugations would be impractical.
